H1114|                        Safety margin multiplied onto scales when auto-saving.
H1115|                        A value > 1 leaves headroom so that inputs with larger

H1131|  --mm-encoder-tp-mode {data,weights}
H1132|                        Indicates how to optimize multi-modal encoder
H1133|                        inference using tensor parallelism (TP).
H1134|                        - `"weights"`: Within the same vLLM engine, split the
H1135|                        weights of each layer across TP ranks. (default TP
H1136|                        behavior)
H1137|                        - `"data"`: Within the same vLLM engine, split the
H1138|                        batched input data across TP ranks to process the data
H1139|                        in parallel, while hosting the full weights on each TP
H1140|                        rank. This batch-level DP is not to be confused with
H1141|                        API request-level DP (which is controlled by `--data-
H1142|                        parallel-size`). This is only supported on a per-model
H1143|                        basis and falls back to `"weights"` if the encoder
H1144|                        does not support DP. (default: weights)
H1145|  --mm-processor-cache-gb MM_PROCESSOR_CACHE_GB
H1146|                        The size (in GiB) of the multi-modal processor cache,
H1147|                        which is used to avoid re-processing past multi-modal
H1148|                        inputs.
H1149|                        This cache is duplicated for each API process and
H1150|                        engine core process, resulting in a total memory usage
H1151|                        of `mm_processor_cache_gb * (api_server_count +
H1152|                        data_parallel_size)`.
H1153|                        Set to `0` to disable this cache completely (not
H1154|                        recommended). (default: 4)
H1155|  --mm-processor-cache-type {lru,shm}

H1314|SchedulerConfig:

H1318|                        If set to False, disable async scheduling. Async

H1322|  --disable-chunked-mm-input, --no-disable-chunked-mm-input

H1324|                        not want to partially schedule a multimodal item. Only
H1325|                        used in V1 This ensures that if a request has a mixed
H1326|                        prompt (like text tokens TTTT followed by image tokens
H1327|                        IIIIIIIIII) where only some image tokens can be

H1334|                        there are multiple type of attention layers like full

H1352|                        prefilled concurrently. Setting this less than

H1391|                        - "fcfs" means first come first served, i.e. requests
H1392|                        are handled in order  of arrival.
H1393|                        - "priority" means requests are handled based on given
H1394|                        priority (lower value means earlier handling) and time

H1396|  --stream-interval STREAM_INTERVAL
H1397|                        The interval (or buffer size) for streaming in terms
H1398|                        of token length. A smaller value (1) makes streaming
H1399|                        smoother by sending each token immediately, while a
H1400|                        larger value (e.g., 10) reduces host overhead and may

H1404|CompilationConfig:
H1405|  Configuration for compilation.
H1406|
H1407|      You must pass CompilationConfig to VLLMConfig constructor.
H1408|      VLLMConfig's post_init does further initialization. If used outside of the
H1409|      VLLMConfig, some fields will be left in an improper state.
H1410|
H1411|      It contains PassConfig, which controls the custom fusion/transformation passes.
H1412|      The rest has three parts:
H1413|
H1414|      - Top-level Compilation control:
H1415|          - [`mode`][vllm.config.CompilationConfig.mode]
H1416|          - [`debug_dump_path`][vllm.config.CompilationConfig.debug_dump_path]
H1417|          - [`cache_dir`][vllm.config.CompilationConfig.cache_dir]
H1418|          - [`backend`][vllm.config.CompilationConfig.backend]
H1419|          - [`custom_ops`][vllm.config.CompilationConfig.custom_ops]
H1420|          - [`splitting_ops`][vllm.config.CompilationConfig.splitting_ops]
H1421|          - [`compile_mm_encoder`][vllm.config.CompilationConfig.compile_mm_encoder]
H1422|      - CudaGraph capture:
H1423|          - [`cudagraph_mode`][vllm.config.CompilationConfig.cudagraph_mode]
H1424|          - [`cudagraph_capture_sizes`]
H1425|          [vllm.config.CompilationConfig.cudagraph_capture_sizes]
H1426|          - [`max_cudagraph_capture_size`]
H1427|          [vllm.config.CompilationConfig.max_cudagraph_capture_size]
H1428|          - [`cudagraph_num_of_warmups`]
H1429|          [vllm.config.CompilationConfig.cudagraph_num_of_warmups]
H1430|          - [`cudagraph_copy_inputs`]
H1431|          [vllm.config.CompilationConfig.cudagraph_copy_inputs]
H1432|      - Inductor compilation:
H1433|          - [`compile_sizes`][vllm.config.CompilationConfig.compile_sizes]
H1434|          - [`compile_ranges_endpoints`]
H1435|              [vllm.config.CompilationConfig.compile_ranges_endpoints]
H1436|          - [`inductor_compile_config`]
H1437|          [vllm.config.CompilationConfig.inductor_compile_config]
H1438|          - [`inductor_passes`][vllm.config.CompilationConfig.inductor_passes]
H1439|          - custom inductor passes
H1440|
H1441|      Why we have different sizes for cudagraph and inductor:
H1442|      - cudagraph: a cudagraph captured for a specific size can only be used
H1443|          for the same size. We need to capture all the sizes we want to use.
H1444|      - inductor: a graph compiled by inductor for a general shape can be used
H1445|          for different sizes. Inductor can also compile for specific sizes,
H1446|          where it can have more information to optimize the graph with fully
H1447|          static shapes. However, we find the general shape compilation is
H1448|          sufficient for most cases. It might be beneficial to compile for
H1449|          certain small batchsizes, where inductor is good at optimizing.
H1450|
H1451|
H1452|  --cudagraph-capture-sizes CUDAGRAPH_CAPTURE_SIZES [CUDAGRAPH_CAPTURE_SIZES ...]
H1453|                        Sizes to capture cudagraph.
H1454|                        - None (default): capture sizes are inferred from vllm
H1455|                        config.
H1456|                        - list[int]: capture sizes are specified as given.
H1457|                        (default: None)
H1458|  --max-cudagraph-capture-size MAX_CUDAGRAPH_CAPTURE_SIZE
H1459|                        The maximum cudagraph capture size.
H1460|                        If cudagraph_capture_sizes is specified, this will be
H1461|                        set to the largest size in that list (or checked for
H1462|                        consistency if specified). If cudagraph_capture_sizes
H1463|                        is not specified, the list of sizes is generated
H1464|                        automatically following the pattern:
H1465|                            [1, 2, 4] + list(range(8, 256, 8)) + list(
H1466|                        range(256, max_cudagraph_capture_size + 1, 16))
H1467|                        If not specified, max_cudagraph_capture_size is set to
H1468|                        min(max_num_seqs*2, 512) by default. This voids OOM in
H1469|                        tight memory scenarios with small max_num_seqs, and
H1470|                        prevents capture of many large graphs (>512) that
H1471|                        would greatly increase startup time with limited
H1472|                        performance benefit. (default: None)
H1473|
H1474|KernelConfig:
H1475|  Configuration for kernel selection and warmup behavior.
H1476|
H1477|  --enable-flashinfer-autotune, --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune
H1478|                        If True, run FlashInfer autotuning during kernel
H1479|                        warmup. (default: None)
H1480|  --ir-op-priority IR_OP_PRIORITY
H1481|                        vLLM IR op priority for dispatching/lowering during
H1482|                        the forward pass. Platform defaults appended
H1483|                        automatically during VllmConfig.__post_init__.
H1484|                        API docs: https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/api/vllm/conf
H1485|                        ig/#vllm.config.IrOpPriorityConfig
H1486|                        Should either be a valid JSON string or JSON keys
H1487|                        passed individually. (default:
H1488|                        IrOpPriorityConfig(rms_norm=[],
H1489|                        fused_add_rms_norm=[]))
H1490|  --linear-backend {aiter,auto,conch,cutlass,deep_gemm,emulation,exllama,fbgemm,flashinfer_cudnn,flashinfer_cutlass,flashinfer_trtllm,machete,marlin,torch,triton}
H1491|                        Backend for quantized linear layer GEMM kernels.
H1492|                        Available options:
H1493|                        - "auto": Automatically select the best backend based
H1494|                        on model and hardware
H1495|                        - "cutlass": Use CUTLASS-based kernels
H1496|                        - "flashinfer_cutlass": Use FlashInfer with CUTLASS
H1497|                        kernels
H1498|                        - "flashinfer_trtllm": Use FlashInfer with TensorRT-
H1499|                        LLM kernels
H1500|                        - "flashinfer_cudnn": Use FlashInfer with cuDNN
H1501|                        kernels
H1502|                        - "marlin": Use Marlin kernels
H1503|                        - "triton": Use Triton-based kernels
H1504|                        - "deep_gemm": Use DeepGEMM kernels
H1505|                        - "torch": Use PyTorch native scaled_mm kernels
H1506|                        - "aiter": Use AMD AITer kernels (ROCm only)
H1507|                        - "machete": Use Machete kernels (mixed-precision)
H1508|                        - "fbgemm": Use FBGEMM kernels
H1509|                        - "conch": Use Conch mixed-precision kernels
H1510|                        - "exllama": Use Exllama mixed-precision kernels

H0185|                        or a commit id. If unspecified, will use the default
H0186|                        version. (default: None)
H0187|  --config-format ['auto', 'hf', 'mistral']
H0188|                        The format of the model config to load:
H0189|                        - "auto" will try to load the config in hf format if
H0190|                        available after trying to load in mistral format.
H0191|                        - "hf" will load the config in hf format.
H0192|                        - "mistral" will load the config in mistral format.
H0193|                        (default: auto)
H0194|  --convert {auto,classify,embed,none}
H0195|                        Convert the model using adapters defined in
H0196|                        [vllm.model_executor.models.adapters][]. The most
H0197|                        common use case is to adapt a text generation model to
H0198|                        be used for pooling tasks. (default: auto)
H0199|  --disable-cascade-attn, --no-disable-cascade-attn
H0200|                        Disable cascade attention for V1. While cascade
H0201|                        attention does not change the mathematical
H0202|                        correctness, disabling it could be useful for
H0203|                        preventing potential numerical issues. This defaults
H0204|                        to True, so users must opt in to cascade attention by
H0205|                        setting this to False. Even when this is set to False,
H0206|                        cascade attention will only be used when the heuristic
H0207|                        tells that it's beneficial. (default: True)
H0208|  --disable-sliding-window, --no-disable-sliding-window
H0209|                        Whether to disable sliding window. If True, we will
H0210|                        disable the sliding window functionality of the model,
H0211|                        capping to sliding window size. If the model does not
H0212|                        support sliding window, this argument is ignored.
H0213|                        (default: False)
H0214|  --dtype {auto,bfloat16,float,float16,float32,half}
H0215|                        Data type for model weights and activations:
H0216|                        - "auto" will use FP16 precision for FP32 and FP16
H0217|                        models, and BF16 precision for BF16 models.
H0218|                        - "half" for FP16. Recommended for AWQ quantization.
H0219|                        - "float16" is the same as "half".
H0220|                        - "bfloat16" for a balance between precision and
H0221|                        range.
H0222|                        - "float" is shorthand for FP32 precision.
H0223|                        - "float32" for FP32 precision. (default: auto)
H0224|  --enable-cumem-allocator, --no-enable-cumem-allocator
H0225|                        Enable the custom cumem allocator to leverage advanced
H0226|                        GPU memory allocation features such as multi-node
H0227|                        NVLink support.
H0228|                        Sleep mode automatically enables this allocator. Only
H0229|                        cuda and hip platforms are supported. (default: False)
H0230|  --enable-prompt-embeds, --no-enable-prompt-embeds
H0231|                        If `True`, enables passing text embeddings as inputs
H0232|                        via the `prompt_embeds` key.
H0233|                        WARNING: The vLLM engine may crash if incorrect shape
H0234|                        of embeddings is passed. Only enable this flag for
H0235|                        trusted users! (default: False)
H0236|  --enable-return-routed-experts, --no-enable-return-routed-experts
H0237|                        Whether to return routed experts. (default: False)
H0238|  --enable-sleep-mode, --no-enable-sleep-mode
H0239|                        Enable sleep mode for the engine (only cuda and hip
H0240|                        platforms are supported). (default: False)
H0241|  --enforce-eager, --no-enforce-eager
H0242|                        Whether to always use eager-mode PyTorch. If True, we
H0243|                        will disable CUDA graph and always execute the model
H0244|                        in eager mode. If False, we will use CUDA graph and
H0245|                        eager execution in hybrid for maximal performance and
H0246|                        flexibility. (default: False)
H0247|  --generation-config GENERATION_CONFIG
H0248|                        The folder path to the generation config. Defaults to
H0249|                        `"auto"`, the generation config will be loaded from
H0250|                        model path. If set to `"vllm"`, no generation config
H0251|                        is loaded, vLLM defaults will be used. If set to a
H0252|                        folder path, the generation config will be loaded from
H0253|                        the specified folder path. If `max_new_tokens` is
H0254|                        specified in generation config, then it sets a server-
H0255|                        wide limit on the number of output tokens for all
H0256|                        requests. (default: auto)
H0257|  --hf-config-path HF_CONFIG_PATH
H0258|                        Name or path of the Hugging Face config to use. If
H0259|                        unspecified, model name or path will be used.
H0260|                        (default: None)
H0261|  --hf-overrides HF_OVERRIDES
H0262|                        If a dictionary, contains arguments to be forwarded to
H0263|                        the Hugging Face config. If a callable, it is called
H0264|                        to update the HuggingFace config. (default: {})
H0265|  --hf-token [HF_TOKEN]
H0266|                        The token to use as HTTP bearer authorization for
H0267|                        remote files . If `True`, will use the token generated
H0268|                        when running `hf auth login` (stored in
H0269|                        `~/.cache/huggingface/token`). (default: None)
H0270|  --io-processor-plugin IO_PROCESSOR_PLUGIN

H0274|                        One or more logits processors' fully-qualified class
H0275|                        names or class definitions (default: None)
H0276|  --logprobs-mode {processed_logits,processed_logprobs,raw_logits,raw_logprobs}
H0277|                        Indicates the content returned in the logprobs and
H0278|                        prompt_logprobs. Supported mode: 1) raw_logprobs, 2)
H0279|                        processed_logprobs, 3) raw_logits, 4)
H0280|                        processed_logits. Raw means the values before applying
H0281|                        any logit processors, like bad words. Processed means
H0282|                        the values after applying all processors, including
H0283|                        temperature and top_k/top_p. (default: raw_logprobs)
H0284|  --max-logprobs MAX_LOGPROBS
H0285|                        Maximum number of log probabilities to return when
H0286|                        `logprobs` is specified in `SamplingParams`. The
H0287|                        default value comes the default for the OpenAI Chat
H0288|                        Completions API. -1 means no cap, i.e. all
H0289|                        (output_length * vocab_size) logprobs are allowed to
H0290|                        be returned and it may cause OOM. (default: 20)
H0291|  --max-model-len MAX_MODEL_LEN
H0292|                        Model context length (prompt and output). If
H0293|                        unspecified, will be automatically derived from the
H0294|                        model config.
H0295|                        When passing via `--max-model-len`, supports
H0296|                        k/m/g/K/M/G in human-readable format. Examples:
H0297|                        - 1k -> 1000
H0298|                        - 1K -> 1024
H0299|                        - 25.6k -> 25,600
H0300|                        - -1 or 'auto' -> Automatically choose the maximum
H0301|                        model length that fits in GPU memory. This will use
H0302|                        the model's maximum context length if it fits,
H0303|                        otherwise it will find the largest length that can be
H0304|                        accommodated.
H0305|                        Parse human-readable integers like '1k', '2M', etc.
H0306|                        Including decimal values with decimal multipliers.
H0307|                        Also accepts -1 or 'auto' as a special value for auto-
H0308|                        detection.
H0309|                            Examples:
H0310|                            - '1k' -> 1,000
H0311|                            - '1K' -> 1,024
H0312|                            - '25.6k' -> 25,600
H0313|                            - '-1' or 'auto' -> -1 (special value for auto-
H0314|                        detection) (default: None)
H0315|  --model MODEL         Name or path of the Hugging Face model to use. It is
H0316|                        also used as the content for `model_name` tag in
H0317|                        metrics output when `served_model_name` is not
H0318|                        specified. (default: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B)
H0319|  --model-impl ['auto', 'terratorch', 'transformers', 'vllm']

H0321|                        - "auto" will try to use the vLLM implementation, if
H0322|                        it exists, and fall back to the Transformers
H0323|                        implementation if no vLLM implementation is available.
H0324|                        - "vllm" will use the vLLM model implementation.

H0367|                        The pool is consumed by the async renderer path (e.g.

H0370|                        rendering, and multimodal preprocessing across

H0372|                        The offline `LLM` entrypoint uses the synchronous

H0384|                        We must set the global seed because otherwise,

H0404|                        Name or path of the Hugging Face tokenizer to use. If

H0407|  --tokenizer-mode ['auto', 'deepseek_v32', 'deepseek_v4', 'hf', 'mistral', 'slow']
H0408|                        Tokenizer mode:
H0409|                        - "auto" will use the tokenizer from `mistral_common`
H0410|                        for Mistral models if available, otherwise it will use
H0411|                        the "hf" tokenizer.
H0412|                        - "hf" will use the fast tokenizer if available.
H0413|                        - "slow" will always use the slow tokenizer.
H0414|                        - "mistral" will always use the tokenizer from
H0415|                        `mistral_common`.
H0416|                        - "deepseek_v32" will always use the tokenizer from
H0417|                        `deepseek_v32`.
H0418|                        - "deepseek_v4" will always use the tokenizer from
H0419|                        `deepseek_v4`.
H0420|                        - "qwen_vl" will always use the tokenizer from
H0421|                        `qwen_vl`.
H0422|                        - Other custom values can be supported via plugins.
H0423|                        To swap the Rust BPE backend that powers HF fast
H0424|                        tokenizers for the
H0425|                        [fastokens](https://github.com/crusoecloud/fastokens)
H0426|                        implementation, set `VLLM_USE_FASTOKENS=1` instead —
H0427|                        that override applies to any mode that loads an HF
H0428|                        fast tokenizer (`hf`, `deepseek_v32`, `deepseek_v4`,

H0437|                        downloading the model and tokenizer. (default: False)

H0439|                        Whether to use FP64 (instead of FP32) for the Gumbel
H0440|                        noise used by the sampler. FP64 reduces the chance of
H0441|                        ties in Gumbel-max sampling at the cost of
H0442|                        significantly lower kernel throughput on most GPUs.
H0443|                        (default: False)
H0444|
H0445|LoadConfig:
H0446|  Configuration for loading the model weights.
H0447|
H0448|  --download-dir DOWNLOAD_DIR
H0449|                        Directory to download and load the weights, default to
H0450|                        the default cache directory of Hugging Face. (default:
H0451|                        None)
H0452|  --ignore-patterns IGNORE_PATTERNS [IGNORE_PATTERNS ...]
H0453|                        The list of patterns to ignore when loading the model.
H0454|                        Default to "original/**/*" to avoid repeated loading
H0455|                        of llama's checkpoints. (default: ['original/**/*'])
H0456|  --load-format LOAD_FORMAT
H0457|                        The format of the model weights to load.
H0458|                        - "auto" will try to load the weights in the
H0459|                        safetensors format and fall back to the pytorch bin
H0460|                        format if safetensors format is not available.
H0461|                        - "pt" will load the weights in the pytorch bin
H0462|                        format.
H0463|                        - "safetensors" will load the weights in the
H0464|                        safetensors format.
H0465|                        - "instanttensor" will load the Safetensors weights on
H0466|                        CUDA devices using InstantTensor, which enables
H0467|                        distributed loading with pipelined prefetching and
H0468|                        fast direct I/O.
H0469|                        - "npcache" will load the weights in pytorch format
H0470|                        and store a numpy cache to speed up the loading.
H0471|                        - "dummy" will initialize the weights with random
H0472|                        values, which is mainly for profiling.
H0473|                        - "tensorizer" will use CoreWeave's tensorizer library
H0474|                        for fast weight loading. See the Tensorize vLLM Model
H0475|                        script in the Examples section for more information.
H0476|                        - "runai_streamer" will load the Safetensors weights
H0477|                        using Run:ai Model Streamer.
H0478|                        - "runai_streamer_sharded" will load weights from pre-
H0479|                        sharded checkpoint files using Run:ai Model Streamer.
H0480|                        - "bitsandbytes" will load the weights using
H0481|                        bitsandbytes quantization.
H0482|                        - "sharded_state" will load weights from pre-sharded
H0483|                        checkpoint files, supporting efficient loading of
H0484|                        tensor-parallel models.
H0485|                        - "gguf" will load weights from GGUF format files
H0486|                        (details specified in https://github.com/ggml-
H0487|                        org/ggml/blob/master/docs/gguf.md).
H0488|                        - "mistral" will load weights from consolidated
H0489|                        safetensors files used by Mistral models.
H0490|                        - "modelexpress" will load weights using ModelExpress.
H0491|                        - Other custom values can be supported via plugins.
H0492|                        (default: auto)
H0493|  --model-loader-extra-config MODEL_LOADER_EXTRA_CONFIG
H0494|                        Extra config for model loader. This will be passed to
H0495|                        the model loader corresponding to the chosen
H0496|                        load_format. (default: {})
H0497|  --pt-load-map-location PT_LOAD_MAP_LOCATION
H0498|                        The map location for loading pytorch checkpoint, to
H0499|                        support loading checkpoints can only be loaded on
H0500|                        certain devices like "cuda", this is equivalent to
H0501|                        `{"": "cuda"}`. Another supported format is mapping
H0502|                        from different devices like from GPU 1 to GPU 0:
H0503|                        `{"cuda:1": "cuda:0"}`. Note that when passed from
H0504|                        command line, the strings in dictionary need to be
H0505|                        double quoted for json parsing. For more details, see
H0506|                        the original doc for `map_location` parameter in
H0507|                        [`torch.load`][] parameter. (default: cpu)
H0508|  --safetensors-load-strategy SAFETENSORS_LOAD_STRATEGY
H0509|                        Specifies the loading strategy for safetensors
H0510|                        weights.
H0511|                        - None (default): Uses memory-mapped (lazy) loading.
H0512|                        When an NFS filesystem is detected and the total
H0513|                        checkpoint size fits within 90%% of available RAM,
H0514|                        prefetching is enabled automatically.
H0515|                        - "lazy": Weights are memory-mapped from the file.
H0516|                        This enables on-demand loading and is highly efficient
H0517|                        for models on local storage. Unlike the default
H0518|                        (None), auto-prefetch on NFS is not performed.
H0519|                        - "eager": The entire file is read into CPU memory
H0520|                        upfront before loading. This is recommended for models
H0521|                        on network filesystems (e.g., Lustre, NFS) as it
H0522|                        avoids inefficient random reads, significantly
H0523|                        speeding up model initialization. However, it uses
H0524|                        more CPU RAM.
H0525|                        - "prefetch": Checkpoint files are read into the OS
H0526|                        page cache before workers load them, speeding up the
H0527|                        model loading phase. Useful on network or high-latency
H0528|                        storage.
H0529|                        - "torchao": Weights are loaded in upfront and then
H0530|                        reconstructed into torchao tensor subclasses. This is
H0531|                        used when the checkpoint was quantized using torchao
H0532|                        and saved using safetensors. Needs `torchao >=
H0533|                        0.14.0`. (default: None)
H0534|  --safetensors-prefetch-block-size SAFETENSORS_PREFETCH_BLOCK_SIZE
H0535|                        Read size in bytes for each safetensors checkpoint
H0536|                        file prefetch.
H0537|                        Parse human-readable integers like '1k', '2M', etc.
H0538|                        Including decimal values with decimal multipliers.
H0539|                            Examples:
H0540|                            - '1k' -> 1,000
H0541|                            - '1K' -> 1,024
H0542|                            - '25.6k' -> 25,600 (default: 16777216)
H0543|  --safetensors-prefetch-num-threads SAFETENSORS_PREFETCH_NUM_THREADS
H0544|                        Number of worker threads used to prefetch safetensors
H0545|                        checkpoint files into the OS page cache when
H0546|                        safetensors prefetching is enabled. (default: 8)
H0547|  --use-tqdm-on-load, --no-use-tqdm-on-load
H0548|                        Whether to enable tqdm for showing progress bar when
H0549|                        loading model weights. (default: True)

H0586|ParallelConfig:
H0587|  Configuration for the distributed execution.
H0588|
H0589|  --all2all-backend {allgather_reducescatter,deepep_high_throughput,deepep_low_latency,flashinfer_all2allv,flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided,flashinfer_nvlink_two_sided,mori_high_throughput,mori_low_latency,naive,nixl_ep,pplx}
H0590|                        All2All backend for MoE expert parallel communication.
H0591|                        Available options:
H0592|                        - "allgather_reducescatter": All2all based on
H0593|                        allgather and reducescatter
H0594|                        - "deepep_high_throughput": Use deepep high-throughput
H0595|                        kernels
H0596|                        - "deepep_low_latency": Use deepep low-latency kernels
H0597|                        - "mori_high_throughput": MoRI EP with InterNodeV1 for
H0598|                        multi-node
H0599|                        - "mori_low_latency": MoRI EP with InterNodeV1LL for
H0600|                        multi-node
H0601|                        - "nixl_ep": Use nixl-ep kernels
H0602|                        - "flashinfer_nvlink_two_sided": Use flashinfer two-
H0603|                        sided kernels for mnnvl
H0604|                        - "flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided": Use flashinfer high-
H0605|                        throughput a2a kernels (default:
H0606|                        allgather_reducescatter)
H0607|  --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size CP_KV_CACHE_INTERLEAVE_SIZE
H0608|                        Interleave size of kv_cache storage while using DCP or
H0609|                        PCP. For `total_cp_rank = pcp_rank * dcp_world_size +
H0610|                        dcp_rank`, and `total_cp_world_size = pcp_world_size *
H0611|                        dcp_world_size`. store interleave_size tokens on
H0612|                        total_cp_rank i, then store next interleave_size
H0613|                        tokens on total_cp_rank i+1. Interleave_size=1: token-
H0614|                        level alignment, where token `i` is stored on
H0615|                        total_cp_rank `i % total_cp_world_size`.
H0616|                        Interleave_size=block_size: block-level alignment,
H0617|                        where tokens are first populated to the preceding
H0618|                        ranks. Tokens are then stored in (rank i+1, block j)
H0619|                        only after (rank i, block j) is fully occupied.
H0620|                        Block_size should be greater than or equal to
H0621|                        cp_kv_cache_interleave_size. Block_size should be
H0622|                        divisible by cp_kv_cache_interleave_size. (default: 1)
H0623|  --cpu-distributed-timeout-seconds CPU_DISTRIBUTED_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
H0624|                        Timeout (in seconds) for cpu communication groups. If

H0766|                        - "linear": Experts are placed in a contiguous manner.
H0767|                        For example, with 4 experts and 2 ranks, rank 0 will
H0768|                        have experts [0, 1] and rank 1 will have experts [2,
H0769|                        3].
H0770|                        - "round_robin": Experts are placed in a round-robin
H0771|                        manner. For example, with 4 experts and 2 ranks, rank
H0772|                        0 will have experts [0, 2] and rank 1 will have
H0773|                        experts [1, 3]. This strategy can help improve load
H0774|                        balancing for grouped expert models with no redundant
H0775|                        experts. (default: linear)

H0845|CacheConfig:
H0846|  Configuration for the KV cache.

H0851|                        construction, always int. (default: None)

H0855|                        `k_scale` and `v_scale` when kv_cache_dtype is fp8. If
H0856|                        `False`, the scales will be loaded from the model

H0858|                        default to 1.0. (default: False)
H0859|  --enable-prefix-caching, --no-enable-prefix-caching
H0860|                        Whether to enable prefix caching. (default: None)
H0861|  --gpu-memory-utilization GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION
H0862|                        The fraction of GPU memory to be used for the model
H0863|                        executor, which can range from 0 to 1. For example, a
H0864|                        value of 0.5 would imply 50% GPU memory utilization.
H0865|                        If unspecified, will use the default value of 0.92.
H0866|                        This is a per-instance limit, and only applies to the
H0867|                        current vLLM instance. It does not matter if you have
H0868|                        another vLLM instance running on the same GPU. For
H0869|                        example, if you have two vLLM instances running on the
H0870|                        same GPU, you can set the GPU memory utilization to
H0871|                        0.5 for each instance. (default: 0.92)
H0872|  --kv-cache-dtype {auto,bfloat16,float16,fp8,fp8_ds_mla,fp8_e4m3,fp8_e5m2,fp8_inc,fp8_per_token_head,int8_per_token_head,nvfp4,turboquant_3bit_nc,turboquant_4bit_nc,turboquant_k3v4_nc,turboquant_k8v4}
H0873|                        Data type for kv cache storage. If "auto", will use
H0874|                        model data type. CUDA 11.8+ supports fp8 (=fp8_e4m3)
H0875|                        and fp8_e5m2. ROCm (AMD GPU) supports fp8 (=fp8_e4m3).
H0876|                        Intel Gaudi (HPU) supports fp8 (using fp8_inc). On
H0877|                        SM70 with the 1Cat Flash-V100 backend enabled, the
H0878|                        user-facing ``fp8`` shorthand resolves to fp8_e5m2 for
H0879|                        compatibility with its optimized KV path; explicit
H0880|                        fp8_e4m3 keeps the upstream E4M3 behavior. Some models
H0881|                        (namely DeepSeekV3.2) default to fp8, set to bfloat16
H0882|                        to use bfloat16 instead, this is an invalid option for
H0883|                        models that do not default to fp8. (default: auto)
H0884|  --kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers KV_CACHE_DTYPE_SKIP_LAYERS [KV_CACHE_DTYPE_SKIP_LAYERS ...]
H0885|                        Layer patterns to skip KV cache quantization. Accepts
H0886|                        layer indices (e.g., '0', '2', '4') or attention type
H0887|                        names (e.g., 'sliding_window'). (default: [])
H0888|  --kv-cache-memory-bytes KV_CACHE_MEMORY_BYTES
H0889|                        Size of KV Cache per GPU in bytes. By default, this is
H0890|                        set to None and vllm can automatically infer the kv
H0891|                        cache size based on gpu_memory_utilization. However,
H0892|                        users may want to manually specify the kv cache memory
H0893|                        size. kv_cache_memory_bytes allows more fine-grain
H0894|                        control of how much memory gets used when compared
H0895|                        with using gpu_memory_utilization. Note that
H0896|                        kv_cache_memory_bytes (when not-None) ignores
H0897|                        gpu_memory_utilization
H0898|                        Parse human-readable integers like '1k', '2M', etc.
H0899|                        Including decimal values with decimal multipliers.
H0900|                            Examples:
H0901|                            - '1k' -> 1,000
H0902|                            - '1K' -> 1,024
H0903|                            - '25.6k' -> 25,600 (default: None)
H0904|  --kv-offloading-backend {lmcache,native}
H0905|                        The backend to use for KV cache offloading. Supported
H0906|                        backends include 'native' (vLLM native CPU
H0907|                        offloading), 'lmcache'. KV offloading is only
H0908|                        activated when kv_offloading_size is set. (default:
H0909|                        native)
H0910|  --kv-offloading-size KV_OFFLOADING_SIZE
H0911|                        Size of the KV cache offloading buffer in GiB. When TP
H0912|                        > 1, this is the total buffer size summed across all
H0913|                        TP ranks. By default, this is set to None, which means
H0914|                        no KV offloading is enabled. When set, vLLM will
H0915|                        enable KV cache offloading to CPU using the
H0916|                        kv_offloading_backend. (default: None)
H0917|  --kv-sharing-fast-prefill, --no-kv-sharing-fast-prefill
H0918|                        This feature is work in progress and no prefill
H0919|                        optimization takes place with this flag enabled
H0920|                        currently.
H0921|                        In some KV sharing setups, e.g. YOCO
H0922|                        (https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.05254), some layers can
H0923|                        skip tokens corresponding to prefill. This flag
H0924|                        enables attention metadata for eligible layers to be
H0925|                        overridden with metadata necessary for implementing
H0926|                        this optimization in some models (e.g. Gemma3n)
H0927|                        (default: False)
H0928|  --mamba-block-size MAMBA_BLOCK_SIZE
H0929|                        Size of a contiguous cache block in number of tokens
H0930|                        for mamba cache. Can be set only when prefix caching
H0931|                        is enabled. Value must be a multiple of 8 to align
H0932|                        with causal_conv1d kernel. (default: None)
H0933|  --mamba-cache-dtype {auto,bfloat16,float16,float32}
H0934|                        The data type to use for the Mamba cache (both the
H0935|                        conv as well as the ssm state). If set to 'auto', the
H0936|                        data type will be inferred from the model config.
H0937|                        (default: auto)
H0938|  --mamba-cache-mode {align,all,none}
H0939|                        The cache strategy for Mamba layers.
H0940|                        - "none": set when prefix caching is disabled.
H0941|                        - "all": cache the mamba state of all tokens at
H0942|                        position i * block_size. This is the default behavior
H0943|                        (for models that support it) when prefix caching is
H0944|                        enabled.
H0945|                        - "align": only cache the mamba state of the last
H0946|                        token of each scheduler step and when the token is at
H0947|                        position i * block_size. (default: none)
H0948|  --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype {auto,bfloat16,float16,float32}
H0949|                        The data type to use for the Mamba cache (ssm state
H0950|                        only, conv state will still be controlled by
H0951|                        mamba_cache_dtype). If set to 'auto', the data type
H0952|                        for the ssm state will be determined by
H0953|                        mamba_cache_dtype. (default: auto)
H0954|  --num-gpu-blocks-override NUM_GPU_BLOCKS_OVERRIDE
H0955|                        Number of GPU blocks to use. This overrides the
H0956|                        profiled `num_gpu_blocks` if specified. Does nothing
H0957|                        if `None`. Used for testing preemption. (default:
H0958|                        None)
H0959|  --prefix-caching-hash-algo {sha256,sha256_cbor,xxhash,xxhash_cbor}
H0960|                        Set the hash algorithm for prefix caching:
H0961|                        - "sha256" uses Pickle for object serialization before
H0962|                        hashing. This is the current default, as SHA256 is the
H0963|                        most secure choice to avoid potential hash collisions.
H0964|                        - "sha256_cbor" provides a reproducible, cross-
H0965|                        language compatible hash. It serializes objects using
H0966|                        canonical CBOR and hashes them with SHA-256.
H0967|                        - "xxhash" uses Pickle serialization with xxHash
H0968|                        (128-bit) for faster, non-cryptographic hashing.
H0969|                        Requires the optional ``xxhash`` package. IMPORTANT:
H0970|                        Use of a hashing algorithm that is not considered
H0971|                        cryptographically secure theoretically increases the
H0972|                        risk of hash collisions, which can cause undefined
H0973|                        behavior or even leak private information in multi-
H0974|                        tenant environments. Even if collisions are still very
H0975|                        unlikely, it is important to consider your security
H0976|                        risk tolerance against the performance benefits before
H0977|                        turning this on.
H0978|                        - "xxhash_cbor" combines canonical CBOR serialization
H0979|                        with xxHash for reproducible hashing. Requires the
H0980|                        optional ``xxhash`` package. (default: sha256)
H0981|
H0982|OffloadConfig:
H0983|  Configuration for model weight offloading to reduce GPU memory usage.
H0984|
H0985|  --cpu-offload-gb CPU_OFFLOAD_GB
H0986|                        The space in GiB to offload to CPU, per GPU. Default
H0987|                        is 0, which means no offloading. Intuitively, this
H0988|                        argument can be seen as a virtual way to increase the
H0989|                        GPU memory size. For example, if you have one 24 GB
H0990|                        GPU and set this to 10, virtually you can think of it
H0991|                        as a 34 GB GPU. Then you can load a 13B model with
H0992|                        BF16 weight, which requires at least 26GB GPU memory.
H0993|                        Note that this requires fast CPU-GPU interconnect, as
H0994|                        part of the model is loaded from CPU memory to GPU
H0995|                        memory on the fly in each model forward pass. This
H0996|                        uses UVA (Unified Virtual Addressing) for zero-copy
H0997|                        access. (default: 0)
H0998|  --cpu-offload-params CPU_OFFLOAD_PARAMS [CPU_OFFLOAD_PARAMS ...]
H0999|                        The set of parameter name segments to target for CPU
H1000|                        offloading. Unmatched parameters are not offloaded. If
H1001|                        this set is empty, parameters are offloaded non-
H1002|                        selectively until the memory limit defined by
H1003|                        `cpu_offload_gb` is reached. Examples:
H1004|                            - For parameter name "mlp.experts.w2_weight":
H1005|                                - "experts" or "experts.w2_weight" will match.
H1006|                                - "expert" or "w2" will NOT match (must be
H1007|                        exact segments).
H1008|                            - A tower component name such as "visual" selects
H1009|                        that complete multimodal tower, including parameters
H1010|                        whose names are relative to the tower module. This
H1011|                        allows distinguishing parameters like "w2_weight" and
H1012|                        "w2_weight_scale". (default: set())
H1013|  --offload-backend {auto,prefetch,uva}
H1014|                        The backend for weight offloading. Options:
H1015|                        - "auto": Selects based on which sub-config has non-
H1016|                        default values (prefetch if offload_group_size > 0,
H1017|                        uva if cpu_offload_gb > 0).
H1018|                        - "uva": UVA (Unified Virtual Addressing) zero-copy
H1019|                        offloading.
H1020|                        - "prefetch": Async prefetch with group-based layer
H1021|                        offloading. (default: auto)
H1022|  --offload-group-size OFFLOAD_GROUP_SIZE
H1023|                        Group every N layers together. Offload last
H1024|                        `offload_num_in_group` layers of each group. Default
H1025|                        is 0 (disabled). Example: group_size=8, num_in_group=2
H1026|                        offloads layers 6,7,14,15,22,23,... Unlike
H1027|                        cpu_offload_gb, this uses explicit async prefetching
H1028|                        to hide transfer latency. (default: 0)
H1029|  --offload-num-in-group OFFLOAD_NUM_IN_GROUP
H1030|                        Number of layers to offload per group. Must be <=
H1031|                        offload_group_size. Default is 1. (default: 1)
H1032|  --offload-params OFFLOAD_PARAMS [OFFLOAD_PARAMS ...]
H1033|                        The set of parameter name segments to target for
H1034|                        prefetch offloading. Unmatched parameters are not
H1035|                        offloaded. If this set is empty, ALL parameters of
H1036|                        each offloaded layer are offloaded. Uses segment
H1037|                        matching: "w13_weight" matches
H1038|                        "mlp.experts.w13_weight" but not
H1039|                        "mlp.experts.w13_weight_scale". (default: set())
H1040|  --offload-prefetch-step OFFLOAD_PREFETCH_STEP
H1041|                        Number of layers to prefetch ahead. Higher values hide
H1042|                        more latency but use more GPU memory. Default is 1.
H1043|                        (default: 1)
H1044|
H1045|MultiModalConfig:
H1046|  Controls the behavior of multimodal models.
H1047|
H1048|  --enable-mm-embeds, --no-enable-mm-embeds
H1049|                        If `True`, enables passing multimodal embeddings: for
H1050|                        `LLM` class, this refers to tensor inputs under
H1051|                        `multi_modal_data`; for the OpenAI-compatible server,
H1052|                        this refers to chat messages with content `"type":
H1053|                        "*_embeds"`.
H1054|                        When enabled with `--limit-mm-per-prompt` set to 0 for
H1055|                        a modality, precomputed embeddings skip count
H1056|                        validation for that modality,  saving memory by not
H1057|                        loading encoder modules while still enabling
H1058|                        embeddings as an input. Limits greater than 0 still
H1059|                        apply to embeddings.
H1060|                        WARNING: The vLLM engine may crash if incorrect shape
H1061|                        of embeddings is passed. Only enable this flag for
H1062|                        trusted users! (default: False)
H1063|  --interleave-mm-strings, --no-interleave-mm-strings
H1064|                        Enable fully interleaved support for multimodal
H1065|                        prompts, while using
H1066|                        --chat-template-content-format=string. (default:
H1067|                        False)
H1068|  --language-model-only, --no-language-model-only
H1069|                        If True, disables all multimodal inputs by setting all
H1070|                        modality limits to 0. Equivalent to setting `--limit-
H1071|                        mm-per-prompt` to 0 for every modality. (default:
H1072|                        False)
H1073|  --limit-mm-per-prompt LIMIT_MM_PER_PROMPT
H1074|                        The maximum number of input items and options allowed
H1075|                        per prompt for each modality.
H1076|                        Defaults to 999 for each modality.
H1077|                        Legacy format (count only): {"image": 16, "video": 2}
H1078|                        Configurable format (with options): {"video":
H1079|                        {"count": 1, "num_frames": 32, "width": 512, "height":
H1080|                        512}, "image": {"count": 5, "width": 512, "height":
H1081|                        512}}
H1082|                        Mixed format (combining both): {"image": 16, "video":
H1083|                        {"count": 1, "num_frames": 32, "width": 512, "height":
H1084|                        512}}
H1085|                        Should either be a valid JSON string or JSON keys
H1086|                        passed individually. (default: {})
H1087|  --media-io-kwargs MEDIA_IO_KWARGS
